summary: Sort values are whitelisted to static fragments, the search term is bound as a parameter, and the page offset is clamped; no injection or abuse path found.
The mandatory payment-verification check is missing from the audit, so the team's GO is unsupported; the release gate prints NO-GO.

GET /projects trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against the session user's orgIds, so any signed-in user can read another organisation's projects and budgets (broken tenant isolation).
RLS is enabled with owner-scoped policies for each operation and anon access revoked, so the id-only client update is constrained by the database; no problem found.
The gate prints CONDITIONAL GO: the only open item is the medium finding AG-007 (no per-account login rate limit), which is accepted with a named owner and approver. GO is not supported.

The middleware matcher covers only /api/admin, and /api/internal/users/[id] DELETE only calls requireSession, so any authenticated member can permanently delete any user account (broken function-level authorisation).
Webhook verifies the signature, requires payment_status paid, and records the event id and grants the plan in one transaction with deduplication; no problem found.

The webhook upgrades the account on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, yet bacs_debit and customer_balance are delayed payment methods, so pro access is granted before payment settles. The event id is also recorded before the update, so a failed update is never retried.

The allow-list check uses startsWith on a URL with no trailing slash (images.partner-cdn.com.evil.example passes) and fetch follows redirects, giving server-side request forgery. There is also no size or content-type validation of the fetched bytes.
The gate prints NO-GO: AG-004 (password reset tokens never expire) is a confirmed high-severity finding that cannot be risk-accepted, so the team's GO is wrong.
The gate prints NO-GO: the ownership evidence was recorded at an older commit (7fd543e) and is stale for the release commit, so a critical control is unverified.
The security definer function document_preview bypasses RLS and is executable by any authenticated user, so anyone can read the title and first 280 characters of any document by id.
All mandatory checks pass with evidence on the audited commit, with no open findings and only the audit file changed since; the gate prints GO.

The transfer view does not validate the amount: a negative value passes the balance check and moves money from the recipient to the sender. Malformed decimals and unknown recipients raise 500s, and wallets are locked in inconsistent order, which risks deadlocks.
The gate prints NO-GO: tenant-isolation, a critical control, has only static evidence and needs runtime evidence on the release commit.

The invoice route uses findFirst, which the scoped client constrains to the session user, so cross-user reads are blocked. The scoped extension covers only findFirst and findMany, which is a latent hardening gap for later code.

The line object spreads the client-supplied input after the server price, so a caller can override unitAmount and name and buy products at any price. The server price must be the only source of the amount.
